BiblicalUsage: This word is a fetter or an anklet, a chain worn on the ankle, and it occurs twice, once as jewellery and once as a trap. Isaiah says the Lord will take away the finery of the daughters of Zion, including their tinkling ornaments, and Proverbs says a young man follows a seductress as an ox goes to the slaughter, or as a fool to the correction of the stocks. The same chain can be an ornament or a prison.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the chains I choose to wear can become the chains that hold me, because beauty without wisdom is a fetter, not a freedom.
